This entry-level AI Engineer will work under close supervision to apply developing technical knowledge in Software Engineering and Generative AI, performing analytic, testing, modeling, and development tasks on smaller projects, and independently on larger, more complex assignments. Perform assigned technical and analytic tasks using established methods and tools, documents methods and results, and escalate novel or ambiguous issues.
Support development of AI-enabled applications and fix straightforward defects under close supervision.
Build and maintain components of LLM-based solutions, including API integrations, prompt and tool/function-calling workflows, and basic RAG pipelines (chunking, embeddings, vector search).
Clean, transform, and analyze data with Python, SQL, and data libraries; build simple ETL steps and visualizations.
Execute assigned test cases, including unit tests and basic retrieval or model evaluations, and help reproduce reported issues.
Serve models and AI services through RESTAPIs and containers, prepare simple configuration changes, and follow deployment runbooks.

Document work and escalation steps in tickets and knowledge base entries.

Problem decomposition, clear communication, reading documentation, collaborating through code review, and explaining results to non-technical people.

Visualization: Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly

APIs and web: requests, REST concepts, FastAPI or Flask to serve models, async basics
Tooling: Git/GitHub, Jupyter, VS Code, Docker basics
Databases SQL (essential): SELECT, WHERE, JOINs, GROUP BY, HAVING, subqueries, CTEs, window functions, indexes, query optimization
Relational databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite; schema design, normalization, primary and foreign keys, transactions
Python connectivity: SQLAlchemy, psycopg2, pandas.read_sql
NoSQL: MongoDB (documents), Redis (caching)
Vector databases (AI-specific): embeddings, similarity search, and tools such as pgvector, Chroma, FAISS, Pinecone
Data pipelines: ETL basics, data warehouses, Airflow concepts
Modern GenAI Skills LLM APIs: Anthropic, OpenAI, structured outputs, tool/function calling
RAG: chunking, embeddings, vector search, retrieval evaluation
Frameworks: LangChain or LlamaIndex (know the basics, but understand what's underneath)
Agents: tool use, multi-step workflows, basic evaluation, and guardrails
MLOps and Deployment Model serving: FastAPI, Docker
Experiment tracking: MLflow, Weights & Biases
Cloud basics: AWS, Azure, or GCP
CI/CD basics, monitoring, model versioning

Purpose :
The Global Connected Logistics and Internet of Things (IoT) Strategy Lead shapes and advances enterprise capabilities that improve visibility, product protection, sustainability and operational performance across the global distribution and logistics network.
This individual contributor role connects business strategy with practical implementation. The individual will lead global initiatives, coordinate requirements and interdependencies across global functions and regions, and partner with Business Technology Solutions (BTS), external providers and operational teams to deploy solutions that are scalable, viable and fit for purpose. There is a travel element to this role, with business meetings in US and Europe, primarily but not limited to those regions.
The successful candidate will bring a combination of strategic thinking, program leadership, commercial and vendor management, and strong cross-functional influence. The position is designed for an experienced supply chain, logistics, technology-enabled transformation professional and does not require deep engineering expertise in every device or platform.
Responsibilities:
Own and continuously develop AbbVie's global connected logistics strategy and multi-year roadmap. This covers shipment visibility, temperature monitoring, RFID, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), geolocation and other monitoring technologies, with the goal of improving product protection, risk management and operational decision-making.
Lead the assessment of emerging logistics technologies and monitoring solutions. Work with regional and functional teams to decide which capabilities to pilot, scale globally, integrate into existing processes or phase out, based on business value and operational fit. Lead priority device and IoT initiatives from opportunity definition through implementation, coordinating requirements, milestones, risks and dependencies to speed up deployment and deliver measurable business value.
Partner with Business Technology Solutions (BTS) and technology partners to turn business requirements into functional, data and integration requirements. Make sure solutions are scalable, supportable and compliant with Good Distribution Practice (GDP).
Manage strategic device, monitoring and technology-provider relationships through performance reviews, roadmap alignment and issue resolution to strengthen service reliability, innovation and value. Own the annual connected logistics budget, including forecasting, spend tracking, vendor invoices, financial reporting and actions to make sure investments deliver expected value.
Partner with Global Supply Chain Security, regional teams, third-party logistics providers and freight forwarders to assess emerging threats. Build product protection and transportation security requirements into logistics strategies, operating models and technology deployments. Implement risk-based security standards and solutions (e.g., TAPA). Lead cross-functional initiatives that improve product security, including programs that make high-value products less visible during transportation and distribution. Together, these reduce theft, diversion and other supply chain risks and strengthen supply chain resilience.
Evolve the working relationship with EH&S on distribution and logistics sustainability. Support Scope 3 emissions guidance, governance and training for emissions self-reporting across markets and third-party partners, and coordinate Product Carbon Footprint requests, to improve data consistency, adoption and alignment with standards.
Engage Distribution Managers, Regional Transportation Management teams and senior cross-functional leaders to address partner performance. Embed requirements, risks and interdependencies into functional, regional and enterprise strategies, enabling clear accountability and timely decisions.

Bachelor’s degree required, in preferred fields such as supply chain, logistics, business, engineering, operations, sustainability, information systems or a related field. An advanced degree or relevant professional certification is preferred.
A minimum of eight years of progressive experience in supply chain, distribution, logistics, technology-enabled transformation, program management, sustainability, security or a related discipline. Experience in pharmaceuticals, life sciences or another regulated industry is preferred but not required.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from strategy through implementation in a global or multi-regional environment.
Experience with one or more of the following areas is preferred: shipment visibility, temperature monitoring, connected devices, IoT, telematics, product or freight security, logistics sustainability, carbon reporting, or vendor-managed technology solutions.
Ability to translate business needs into clear requirements and partner effectively with technology teams on data, integration, system and architecture considerations without requiring hands-on engineering ownership.
Experience managing external vendors, logistics providers or strategic partners, including performance management, governance and issue resolution.
Strong stakeholder leadership and influencing skills, with the ability to build alignment across senior leaders, regional teams, functional experts and external partners without direct authority.
Sound judgment and structured problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate tradeoffs, manage ambiguity and recommend pragmatic paths forward.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information into concise, executive-ready recommendations and updates.
Working knowledge of project and program management practices, data-driven performance management and change adoption. Familiarity with supply chain platforms, analytics or reporting tools is beneficial.

The Customer Logistics Planner is the execution and control hub for outbound shipments in the Gaucho third-party manufacturing model. The role coordinates end-to-end order and shipment execution from second-leg stock transport order creation through shipment departure, documentation archiving, exception resolution and stakeholder communication.
The planner helps protect supply continuity and customer service by maintaining accurate system transactions, compliant shipping documentation, timely visibility and early escalation of risks.
The Customer Logistics Planner owns shipment execution and visibility within the Shipment CoE, while Transportation retains ownership of carrier strategy, transportation procurement and carrier management.
Key responsibilities
Order and delivery execution: Create and manage second-leg STOs and outbound deliveries in SAP; update weights and measurements using the Nota Fiscal; create packing lists; post goods issue for departed shipments; and provide accurate shipment data to support commercial invoicing.
Shipping and export documentation: Prepare pro forma invoices and other shipment documentation for customs and payment purposes; check completeness and compliance; and archive final shipping documentation in the designated repository.
Shipment control and visibility: Maintain shipping forecasts and master arrival schedules, monitor open orders and deliveries, review allocation issues and blocks, and escalate overdue or at-risk shipments.
Exception management: Coordinate resolution of shipment delays, booking constraints, documentation gaps, complaints, discrepancies, complex lane requirements and urgent business requests, working with Transportation and other relevant functions as needed.
Stakeholder coordination: Coordinate daily with the third-party manufacturer, Global Supply Planning, Transportation, affiliates, Global Trade Compliance, Finance, Quality, Planning and other supply chain partners. Engage with carriers as required in line with the agreed Transportation interface and operating model.
Affiliate and customer service: Provide timely updates and pre-alert information, align around holiday schedules and market-specific requirements, and support affiliates with complex export and transportation needs.
Performance and governance: Support operational and carrier performance reviews by providing shipment data, issue trends and execution insights, together with KPI reporting, month-end activities, audit readiness, process controls and the Calendar of Discipline.
Continuous improvement: Identify process gaps, improve standard work, strengthen controls and visibility, and contribute to scalable solutions as shipment volumes and regional complexity increase. Support stabilization and continuous improvement of new operating models as processes and interfaces mature.
Key interfaces
Internal: Shipment CoE, Transportation, Global Supply Planning, Finance, Global Trade Compliance, Quality Assurance, Planning, manufacturing and distribution teams, and commercial affiliates.
External: Third-party manufacturer, freight forwarders, service providers, destination-market partners and carriers, with carrier engagement coordinated through Transportation where applicable.
Bachelor's or master's degree, preferably in Logistics, Supply Chain, Operations, Business Management, or a related discipline.
Minimum three years of relevant experience in logistics, customer logistics, order management, supply chain execution, or a comparable environment.
Hands-on ERP experience, preferably SAP, including order, delivery, shipment, or inventory transactions.
Experience with international shipping documentation, export processes, customs-related requirements, and cross-functional stakeholder coordination.
Fluent written and spoken English; additional languages are an advantage for international market support.

The Biotherapeutics Production group at AbbVie is seeking an experienced protein expression scientist to join a fast paced, high throughput, large scale (1 to 200L) mammalian cell culture expression group. title: Scientist, Systems Immunology
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. AbbVie Immunology is expanding its discovery Systems Immunology team in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The team is focused on identifying new targets for the treatment of autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases through computational analysis of human disease tissue-derived datasets and validating targets using humanized experimental approaches.
We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled individual to join our team as a Computational Immunology Scientist. The successful candidate will develop and implement computational approaches to understand disease biology and drug responses using high-throughput molecular profiling data. This role will involve integrating single-cell RNA-seq, scATAC-seq, TCR/BCR repertoire, bulk RNA-seq, and Olink proteomics data to characterize disease-associated cell states, investigate gene regulatory networks, and identify therapeutic opportunities.
The scientist will work in a multidisciplinary team analyzing multiomics datasets to derive insights into immunological diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets relevant to patient cohorts and AbbVie pipeline drugs. The candidate will also contribute to scientific conference presentations, peer-reviewed publications of translational findings, new drug applications, and regulatory filings. If you are passionate about translating complex biological data into actionable insights and advancing personalized medicine, we encourage you to apply.
This position will be based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and requires passion, attention to detail, prior hands-on experience, and teamwork.
Key Responsibilities:
Analyze scRNA-seq, and CITE-seq, datasets, including quality control, integration, clustering, and cell-type and cell-state annotation.
Integrate patient cohorts with reference atlases and perform differential expression, abundance, and pathway analyses, accounting for donor variation and study design.
Analyze scATAC-seq data to identify differential accessibility, transcription factor motifs, and candidate regulatory programs; integrate accessibility with gene expression to infer peak-to-gene relationships.
Analyze TCR/BCR repertoires, including clonotype assignment, clonal expansion, diversity, V(D)J usage, and sharing across tissues or time points; link clonotypes to matched single-cell profiles.
Analyze bulk RNA-seq and Olink proteomics data and integrate multiomics findings to support target prioritization and biomarker hypotheses; maintain documented, version-controlled workflows and evaluate methods using cloud or high-performance computing.
Collaborate with internal and external scientists to prioritize hypotheses for validation, communicate findings and limitations, and contribute to presentations and publications.
BS or MS degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, genomics, biostatistics, computer science, or a related quantitative field with typically 5-7+ years (BS) or 2-5+ years (MS) of relevant experience.
Hands-on scRNA-seq analysis experience or experience with scATAC-seq or TCR/BCR analysis, with interest in developing expertise across both.
Proficiency in Python and/or R and experience working in Linux-based computing environments.
Experience with commonly used bioinformatics tools and frameworks such as Scanpy, AnnData, Cell Ranger, scvi-tools, DESeq2, GSEA, WGCNA, or related methods.
Working knowledge of statistical analysis, multiple-testing correction, batch effects, and biological replication in high-dimensional datasets.
Ability to translate biological questions into analyses, interpret and communicate results critically, collaborate effectively, and manage multiple priorities with attention to detail.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, manage multiple priorities, and deliver high-quality analyses with attention to detail.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience analyzing Olink or other high-plex proteomics datasets.
Experience with CITE-seq, ATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, or integrative multi-omics analysis.
Experience building or benchmarking machine-learning models, including convolutional neural networks, autoencoders, generative models, transfer learning, or foundation models.
Experience with cloud or high-performance computing, including AWS and/or SLURM.
Understanding of immunology and inflammatory disease biology; experience supporting target discovery with experimental teams and communicating research through presentations, publications, or reports.
Evidence of scientific communication through presentations, posters, publications, technical reports, or related research contributions.

location: Seattle; Remote Washington; San Francisco; Remote Oregon; San Jose; Los Angeles; Remote California
description:
About the Role
The Global Microsoft GTM Lead owns the strategic partnership between Adobe and Microsoft. You will set and execute the joint go-to-market strategy, expand customer relationships and Azure Marketplace adoption, and align executives, field teams, product, and marketing across both companies. As the primary liaison between Adobe and Microsoft, you are accountable for revenue growth, cloud adoption, seller enablement, and delivery of the joint business plan.
This is a build role. The partner ecosystem is early, programs are still being designed, and you will work across three organizations (including SIs) whose incentives on any given deal don’t always align. You will help shape how frontier AI technology reaches the enterprise through the services ecosystem.
Key Responsibilities
Strategy and Execution
Own the end-to-end GTM strategy and operation of the alliance, prioritizing high-value enterprise opportunities and driving revenue through Microsoft field engagement and joint co-sell motions.
Decide where to concentrate investment across the partner portfolio, and make the case to stop investing where returns are not there.
Provide market intelligence and competitive insight on the partner ecosystem to inform product and commercial strategy.
Partner with Adobe’s alliances, sales, partner marketing, and regional cloud teams to keep the motion consistent globally while regions execute locally.
Governance and Operating Cadence
Lead the alliance operating rhythm: annual business planning, executive business reviews (EBRs), and quarterly and monthly business reviews (QBRs, MBRs).
Develop and manage annual business plans, growth initiatives, and partnership objectives with Adobe and Microsoft leaders.
Build scalable processes for partnership operations, including escalation management, business reviews, and reporting.
Maintain executive engagement plans, stakeholder maps, governance frameworks, and action tracking.
Prepare executive-ready materials, including strategic updates, account reviews, business cases, win stories, and operating plans.
Performance and Measurement
Own executive dashboards, scorecards, pipeline reviews, forecasting, and performance reporting for both leadership teams.
Define, track, and report alliance KPIs: revenue influence, Azure consumption, Marketplace performance, co-sell activity, customer adoption, migration outcomes, and executive engagement.
Monitor partnership health, flag risks and opportunities, and recommend actions to accelerate growth. Draw on data from sales, finance, marketing, product, engineering, and customer success.
Drive operational excellence through process improvement, reporting automation, and business insights.
Field Activation and Marketplace Growth
Expand Azure Marketplace adoption and manage incentive programs, sponsorships, funding, and co-sell benefits.
Activate Microsoft field teams around Adobe priorities and strategic accounts to accelerate adoption of Co-Worker/Copilot, AMA Launch, CSC on Azure, Adobe Brand Visibility, and relevant third-party partner solutions.
Deliver enablement programs, workshops, and GTM guidance so Adobe solutions are positioned effectively in Microsoft customer conversations, driving consumption through Adobe workloads and modern workplace initiatives.
Support regional sales leadership meetings, pipeline management, reporting, and field enablement alongside the Adobe Microsoft Alliance team.
Marketing and Thought Leadership
Work with Adobe and Microsoft sales and marketing teams to develop assets, events, and customer programs.
Support customer references, success stories, analyst engagements, and executive communications.
Present at industry events, customer workshops, and alliance forums, positioning Adobe as a strategic cloud, AI, and digital workspace partner in the Microsoft ecosystem.
Cross-Functional and Product Alignment
Align executives, product teams, the Adobe-Microsoft partner team, sales leadership, and marketing around year-over-year revenue growth.
Coordinate stakeholders across sales, marketing, product, engineering, finance, and operations to drive accountability on strategic initiatives.
Work with product management and engineering to align Adobe and Microsoft roadmaps and secure opportunities and funding for integration, innovation, and joint solutions.
Represent customer and Microsoft requirements in product planning, using adoption metrics and usage telemetry to measure impact and business value.
Qualifications
Education: MBA or equivalent practical experience.
Experience: 10-15+ years in global technology partner management, GTM, and partner sales leadership, working directly with enterprise customers, cloud service providers, C-level executives, and sales leaders.
Industry knowledge: Enterprise software sales and operations, competitive landscapes, and cloud marketplace business models.
Alliance expertise: Deep knowledge of alliance management, co-sell metrics and motions, and partner programs, ideally within the Microsoft ecosystem.
Hyperscaler partnerships: Experience developing GTM strategy and co-sell programs with the largest hyperscalers.
Strategic agreements: Experience planning and executing multi-year partner sales and product agreements.
Influence and collaboration: Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and drive execution across matrix organizations, including sales, product, and marketing.
Communication: Exceptional communication skills and executive presence, with the ability to influence senior internal and external stakeholders.
Adaptability: Comfortable in fast-paced, ambiguous environments across time zones, with a focus on measurable outcomes.

description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
Airbnb is powered by our Guests & Hosts. Our teams work on everything from driving improvements for the end-to-end Host and Guest experience to launching new product verticals from the ground up. Our job is to build world-class, comprehensive platforms and features to create high quality experiences for our outstanding guest and host communities.
Within our Guest & Host organization is the Communication and Connectivity team. This role will focus on one area in our connectivity branch, which is responsible for evolving our integration platform to connect 3rd party property management systems at scale.
The Difference You Will Make:
Lead the evolution of a world-class supply integration platform to take the third-party supply ecosystem to a new level
Set the third-party supply growth strategy and technical roadmap in collaboration with the cross-functional leadership team
Set the technical and AI strategy for the platform, staying at the forefront of technology to improve its capability, efficiency, quality, and scalability
Build, grow, and mentor a high-performing engineering team, providing people and technical leadership across multiple projects
Partner with cross-functional leaders as the senior technical voice, aligning priorities and driving delivery

As a Senior Engineering Manager, you will be highly cross functional and partner with senior leadership across Data Science, Product, and our Business Development teams to align strategies, define multi-year technical roadmaps, set and execute on iterative milestones.
Work directly with business and third-party partners to select the right partnerships, deliver high-quality integrations, and ensure the continuous reliability and performance of each partner
Lead, coach and develop a team of engineers, helping them grow their careers, technical expertise, and collaboration skills.

12+ years of overall engineering experience with 5+ years managing a team in a fast paced, high growth tech environment
BS, MS or PhD in Computer Science or related field
Significant experience navigating many internal partners across multiple teams, driving the strategy and alignment to move the business forward. This includes navigating dependencies, competing priorities, and demonstrating curiosity while providing direction
Experience building, leading, and architecting full-stack products and systems at enterprise scale with a great impact
Experience in applying modern artificial intelligence technologies to products and development cycles
Technical leadership: hands on experience leading project teams, setting technical direction and strategy, and working cross functionally with Product and Data Science teams
Strong communication and collaboration skills. Examples of working across teams, influencing others, assessing the tradeoffs of different approaches,  and communicating technical initiatives to both technical and non-technical teams.

description:
The Mission
AWS customers trust us with their sensitive data. We are building AWS Support Authorization, the mechanism that puts the decision about Support access in the customer's hands. The customer defines what AWS personnel may do, scoped to their own resources and bound to their open support case, and sees the resulting access in CloudTrail. We are looking for a Principal Product Manager - Technical to own that product and define the experience every AWS service presents when it needs a customer's permission. Your work will change how AWS asks for access to customer content across its services, and it will carry to customer data protection at industry scale.
What You'll Own
You own the approval product end to end, from the API and console surfaces to the evidence a customer keeps afterward and the requirements AWS service teams build to. You define the approval model and the experience a customer moves through when AWS asks for permission, you set the success metrics, and you read the usage data to learn whether customers trust the control enough to use it. You partner with AWS Support, service teams, and Legal on what approval means in each operational context, and with GTM, Marketing, and PR on the strategy, messaging, and themes AWS uses to talk about customer approval and operator access, so what a customer hears matches what they find in the product.
The Product Challenge
A customer with an open case wants two things at once. They want to decide who touches their data, and they want their problem fixed now. Approval that feels meaningful to give takes effort to give, and the person paying that effort is already waiting on help. Designing an experience a customer trusts, can get through without stalling their own case, and recognizes whichever AWS service they called about is the center of this role. There is no predetermined answer. You define it, and you take the definition to the service teams that build to it.
The Impact
Your work will have CISO-level visibility. You write the decision narratives and investment proposals that set product direction, and you take them to VPs and the CISO. You set requirements for engineering teams that do not report to you, and you earn adoption by being right and being clear. You represent the product directly to customers in financial services, healthcare, and the public sector, who ask hard questions about who at a provider can reach their data. As the capability reaches the rest of AWS, the experience you define becomes the way AWS asks for a customer's permission.
What We're Looking For
You are a product manager with real technical depth and a long view. You think about what this product should be two and three years out, before customers have put words to the requirement, and about what it says about AWS to a customer deciding where to run a regulated workload. You have defined a platform product that other engineering teams adopted and built on without reporting to you, and you did it by writing requirements clear enough to survive contact with engineering. You read an authorization or access-control architecture closely enough to know which models a given service can implement. You work across the whole AWS portfolio, where services differ in how they are built and operated, and you guide VPs and directors on where the product goes next. You hold opinions about security and permissions experiences and you back them with customer evidence. You set strategy while the customer requirements are still being discovered, and you own the call when security and customer convenience pull against each other. You have worked with product marketing and PR on positioning a capability whose value is trust, and you have sat across from a regulated customer and answered hard questions about provider access. You develop other product managers as the product grows past what one person owns.
Key job responsibilities
Own the customer experience for AWS Support Authorization end to end: how a customer learns Support needs access, what the request tells them, how they decide, what proof they keep afterward. Define the consent model, covering approval granularity, defaults, duration, revocation behavior mid-case, and the evidence a customer receives. Set the requirements AWS services build to as the capability reaches the rest of AWS, and decide which elements a service team may shape to its own workflow. Own the API and console product surfaces. Define the success metrics and read the usage data to learn how customers respond to consent requests. Partner with AWS Support and service teams on what consent means in each operational context, and bring in Legal on the commitments the product makes to customers. Partner with GTM, Marketing, and PR on how AWS positions customer consent and operator access. Write the decision narratives and investment proposals that set product direction and present them to VP and CISO-level leadership. Represent the product directly to customers. Mentor PMTs and contribute to PMT assessments.
A day in the life
The AWS Proactive Security team builds the controls that protect customer data at scale. You start the day in the usage data, looking at how customers responded to consent requests over the past week and what that says about the experience. You meet a service team preparing to adopt Support Authorization, work through how consent should present for their access patterns, and decide what their integration can and cannot vary. title: Sr. Product Manager Tech - AWS, Global System Integration
description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. We keep the cloud running: the data centers and all the power, cooling, networking, and structural systems behind them.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the business case for each product or platform you carry, defining the cost target, customer need, constraint set, and measure of success.
- Set and defend the constraint box Engineering solves within, drawing the cost, schedule, sustainability, and buildability limits from the business case.
- Govern design change, the largest controllable cost driver, by being the test every proposed change passes or fails on whether it earns its cost and schedule hit against the case.
- Own the full chain from design decision to delivered megawatt.
- Prioritize across the portfolio when new demand arrives, deciding what gets staffed and what slips, naming the cost of leaving a product understaffed, and tying every staffing ask to a specific product and tier so the tradeoffs stay explicit and documented.
- Author and defend the business case in the operating plans, reviews, and strategy papers that release capital, and turn repeatable product judgment into decision-support mechanisms the organization can run without you.
A day in the life
You start by checking the products you own against their cases: is cost on target, are dates holding without burning buffer, are design errors trending down. In a design review, you judge not the engineering but whether a proposed change earns its cost and schedule hit and whether anyone has signed off the departure. When new demand lands, you decide what it displaces and write that tradeoff down so it is traceable. You draft a business case for an operating-plan review, coach a PM through theirs, and close an open sign-off before it re-opens first principles.

description:

Serviceability is the ability to maintain, repair, and manage infrastructure assets efficiently throughout their lifecycle, encompassing maintenance standards, spares management, training and certifications, operational readiness, and the systematic use of data and automation to prevent disruptions and drive continuous improvement.
We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to support serviceability for water systems across our data centers. Water quality management is a critical and fast-growing area of data center operations, where evaporative cooling, condenser water, and makeup water systems must be kept safe, compliant, and reliable to protect both people and infrastructure. This role will define how water systems are sampled, maintained, and kept within regulatory compliance as we scale from early programs to a global fleet, with a focus on proactively catching water quality issues before they drive equipment degradation or infrastructure downtime.
What you will do:
You will own the serviceability program for water systems across the fleet. You will write and maintain preventive maintenance (PM) guidelines for water sampling across all water bodies in our data centers, such as cooling towers, condenser and chilled water loops, evaporative systems, and storage tanks, making sure these guidelines meet regulatory and environmental compliance requirements across every region we operate in. You will build these guidelines with Operations, Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO), Industrial Hygiene, Environmental, and water treatment vendors. You will set the serviceability framework for water systems so that sampling, treatment, and remediation happen on time and water quality issues are caught proactively rather than after they affect equipment or availability. You will partner with Finance on labor analyses that turn sampling and treatment needs into staffing plans. You will work with Field Engineering to lead root cause analyses on water quality and equipment findings, and you will make sure the lessons feed back into PM standards and procedures. You will work with Operations and site teams to build operational readiness plans for new sites, then track readiness so every site is sampling and compliant from day one. You will also run field trials and stakeholder workshops to validate procedures, collect feedback and drive continuous improvement.

Write and maintain PM guidelines for water sampling across all water bodies, ensuring they meet regulatory and environmental compliance, working with Operations, DCEO, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental, and vendors

Build operational readiness plans with Operations and site teams, and track readiness as new sites deploy
Run field trials and stakeholder workshops to validate procedures and collect operational feedback
Keep serviceability standards current as the fleet grows and new equipment, regulations, and vendors are introduced
Use data and metrics to measure program health, prioritize effort and report progress
Write narratives (one to six pages) and present to Director-level leadership
Travel up to 10–15%

Foundational understanding of gate-level signal integrity concepts, including crosstalk glitch noise and static timing analysis (STA).

title: Senior Software Engineer — Service Observability & Detection

Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The last mile delivery driver handles the final leg of delivery and installation getting Base Power battery systems to members' homes on time and setting them up right. Day-to-day work includes operating a 26ft box truck with a passenger team member, loading products, driving a route, installing ground-mounted batteries systems, and keeping accurate delivery records in our in-house app. 

What You'll Do

 - Deliveries: Transport and hand off products to residential and business addresses safely and on time

 - Equipment operation: Use electric pallet jacks and dollies to move pallets in and out of the truck

 - Battery installation: Stack batteries, complete light assembly, and commission the app-based system at each site

 - Member interaction: Answer or direct questions and address concerns on-site with clear, professional communication

 - Site cleanup: Remove all packaging and debris from the member's property before leaving

 - Route management: Follow efficient routes to hit delivery windows consistently

 - Vehicle upkeep: Keep the delivery vehicle clean and organized. Run basic maintenance checks before each shift

 - Delivery logging: Record delivery times, addresses, product, and notes accurately in the delivery app

 - Inventory: Assist with loading and unloading. Run truck cycle counts when requested

 - Safety: Follow all driving and product-handling safety protocols

 - Issue reporting: Flag delays, damages, missing items, or road issues to dispatch or a supervisor promptly

 

What You'll Bring

 - Valid driver's license with a clean record

 - Ability to pass a DOT physical

 - Experience driving box trucks, vans, or commercial vehicles preferred

 - Strong communication skills and comfort working directly with members

 - Able to learn and use apps, systems, and tech platforms required for the role

 - Able to lift and carry 50+ lbs

 - Comfortable navigating routes using GPS or mapping software

 - Self-directed and reliable in a fast-paced environment

 - Basic vehicle maintenance knowledge

 - Able to work outdoors year-round in all weather conditions

 

About the Team

Our delivery and warehouse team ensures solar batteries, inverters, and installation equipment reach residential job sites on time and in perfect condition. We handle the last-mile logistics that determine whether thousands of families get their clean energy systems installed on schedule. Your work directly impacts our ability to scale—every efficient route, properly kitted job, and damage-free delivery means another home powered by renewable energy instead of the grid.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.

We are looking for a tenured, highly technical Product Analytics Sr. Manager to serve as a key architect for our experimentation and product strategy. Your work will help partner teams prioritize what to build, set goals, and understand their impact.
Your work will directly influence product direction, investment decisions, and the product vision for the Retail Bank. You will help drive product led growth by employing a varied toolkit of rigorous analytical approaches, different statistical methodologies, and frameworks to surface insights on new and exciting opportunities and challenges. Key Responsibilities
Product Strategy & Roadmap Influence: Partner closely with Product Management and Engineering to identify high-leverage growth opportunities. Translate complex behavioral data and user funnels into actionable product recommendations and feature requirements.
Experimentation & Causal Inference: Serve as internal authority on experimentation and causal inference. Define and enforce the standards for randomization, power analysis, and conversion window modeling. Design, analyze, and interpret complex A/B/n tests using advanced statistical techniques (randomization, power calculations, variance reduction, quasi-experiments) to isolate true customer incrementality.
Hands-On Technical Execution: Query, clean, and transform massive, complex datasets using SQL, Python, or R. Develop statistical models, user segmentation frameworks, and exploratory analysis to uncover engagement patterns.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Alignment: Drive alignment across cross-functional partners (Product, Tech, Research, Finance). Facilitate peer review gates to maintain rigorous analytical integrity and establish standardized KPI frameworks.
Data Storytelling & Executive Communication: Synthesize multi-faceted data insights into clear, strategic narratives. Able to influence audiences beyond vanity metrics to focus on underlying customer value and long-term business impact.
What success looks like
Proven Track Record: A seasoned analytical expert with significant experience in high-velocity product environments (e.g., e-commerce, fin-tech, or SaaS). You have navigated complex, ambiguous zero-to-one challenges and delivered clear outcomes.
Technical Mastery: Fluency in SQL and Python is a baseline requirement. Deep expertise in statistical modeling, DoE (Design of Experiments), and causal inference methodologies is critical.
Influencer Mindset: You possess strong executive communication skills and the ability to drive agreement through intellect and interpersonal negotiation rather than hierarchy. You can explain the "why" behind a complex statistical result to non-technical partners.
Product Sense: You understand how digital products are built, instrumented, and scaled. You know when to utilize centralized, self-serve experimentation tools versus when a high-bar, gate-kept methodology is required.

The Lead Software Engineer applies advanced knowledge of software engineering principles, modern architectural patterns, and emerging delivery methodologies to drive the technical direction of complex, distributed software platforms at the Release Train level. Serving as an influential participant in solution discovery and architectural decision-making, this role leads milestone and epic-level technical solutioning across the value stream’s product portfolio; defines reference implementations and engineering standards for the teams it supports; and partners across release trains to ensure architectural coherence as the platform evolves. This role applies effective influence and collaboration—without formal management authority—across Engineering, Product, Architecture, and SRE to drive decisions and unblock delivery throughout the software development lifecycle.
The Lead Software Engineer takes the lead on difficult technical problem-solving and cross-team coordination, predicts and documents potential architectural risks and constraints, and leverages AI-assisted engineering tooling to compound their own and the broader engineering organization’s productivity. As engineering teams increasingly rely on AI-generated code, the Lead Software Engineer serves as a thought leader in evolving solution discovery practices to meet this shift — defining how architectural intent, integration contracts, and implementation patterns are embedded into spec-driven development workflows and AI coding agent configurations, ensuring technical direction is established at the point of generation rather than discovered through downstream rework.

Defines technical standards and reference implementations for the value stream’s product architectures, ensuring consistency across the portfolio and clear patterns for delivery teams to follow.
Partners with Value Stream Architects, peer Release Train level engineers, and adjacent release trains to align technical direction, surface architectural risks, and drive cross-train decisions before they become delivery blockers.
Identifies teams with architectural drift, technical debt, or capability gaps and embeds to lead remediation — coaching on patterns, driving solution design, and verifying technical readiness before delivery commitments are made.
Drives adoption of spec-driven development across the value stream’s delivery teams, embedding architectural intent and integration contracts into the artifacts AI coding agents and engineers consume — rather than relying on post-implementation correction.
Serves as the right hand to the incident commander during production incidents, providing technical depth across the value stream’s product surface, accelerating diagnosis, and driving decisive remediation.
Remains the tip of the spear on emerging engineering technologies — including AI-assisted development, spec-driven workflows, and modern integration patterns — through hands-on adoption, then transfers that capability to delivery teams through structured mentorship and reference work.
Identifies architectural risks within the value stream’s technology footprint, defines mitigation strategies, and drives them to documented decisions that set forward-looking technical direction.

Hands-on experience leading technical solution discovery for complex initiatives, producing specifications and architectural artifacts that other engineers execute against.

description:
About the Team
DashMart is a local-fulfillment center owned and operated by DoorDash, offering customers household essentials and other items to their doorsteps with speed, reliability, and quality.
About the Role
In this role, you’ll work within a 5-15k sq ft distribution center, will assist in leading the local warehouse operating team, and in some locations, includes preparing food in a light-prep kitchen, and help the Site Manager ensure we maintain high quality for our customers.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Lead: You’ll demonstrate compassion and commitment to inclusivity as you lead a team of hourly Operations Associates and Shift Leads. You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your site, helping your team to navigate new initiatives and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners.
Operate: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results in one or more specific focus areas or a specific shift for your site. To achieve your performance targets, you’ll drive success through effective scheduling and by executing inventory management processes and deploying best practices from across the network. You’ll engage cross-functional partners as needed for support.
Strategize: Within the focus area(s) assigned by your Site Manager, you’ll analyze data and make strategic recommendations and execute actions regarding resource allocation, workflow, warehouse organization and when to engage cross-functional partners. You may also lead some process improvement projects.
Delight: We are customer-obsessed. You’ll coach and empower your team to provide a highly quality customer experience with every order. Quality metrics such as order accuracy and fulfillment speed will be key measurements of success for your team. You’ll also work cross-functionally with central teams from our inventory to training teams to ensure your team has the tools and resources they’ll need to deliver.
We’re excited about you because…
You’re a proven leader. You have managed high-performance teams of 5+ employees with successful performance and employee development outcomes.
You relish ownership. You’re excited to have ownership in a new and rapidly growing business. No problem is too big or too small for you, and you’re ready to show up however needed for your team.
You solve problems from first principles.   You’re excited to solve problems in innovative ways, and you resist “this is how it’s always been done” thinking.
You’re unafraid of ambiguity.   Rapid change and learning is exciting to you, and you thrive in ambiguous, startup environments.
You’re analytical . You let data win arguments. You are a data-first problem solver and you have experience using Excel or Google Sheets to analyze data, including using basic formulas and creating pivot tables.
You have 3+ years’ experience : In Operations, Warehouse Logistics, Customer Service, Retail Management, Fulfillment, or related field
You have 1+ years of experience managing a team

title: Manager, Federal Affairs
description:
About The Team
DoorDash’s Public Policy & Social Impact Team advocates for legislation that supports the health of our business and empowers our community of Dashers, local business partners, and consumers. Through our advocacy on cutting-edge public policy issues and the programs that we develop, we are shaping the future of local economies. This unique team combines direct engagement with policymakers at all levels of government, advocacy campaigns, policy research and analysis, and programs to promote equity, safety, and sustainability.
About The Role
DoorDash is hiring a proven Federal Affairs Manager to help shape our public policy strategy and execution, independently assist with integrated issue management campaigns, and build lasting and positive relationships with federal public policy stakeholders. Based in Washington DC, you’ll be a key team member supporting the work of the Federal Affairs team and work closely with Public Affairs, Communications, Legal, and other business functions. You will report to the Head of Federal Affairs.
At DoorDash, excellence in Federal Affairs means that…
When our federal government relations stakeholders are considering public policies that could impact DoorDash and the lives and livelihoods of Dashers, merchants, and consumers, we are early, active, and influential participants in the policy debate.
We are at the table and impactful because we are active, credible, reliable, and ethical leaders. Our stakeholders understand and appreciate that DoorDash is a trusted partner and is committed to bringing positive change to the communities we serve. The commitments we make and the relationships we build are real.
We’ve proactively identified policy priorities, emerging threats, and opportunities and are actively advancing favorable policy solutions while also investing time and resources into developing real and long-term relationships with our stakeholders.
You’re excited about this opportunity because…
You are a key player in DoorDash’s connection between federal public policy stakeholders and advancing a mission critical, proactive policy agenda.
You are excited to develop and build new internal processes to support the team and accelerate our impact.
You can effectively coordinate and execute tasks within multiple, complex public policy campaigns.

title: Manager, Lease Accounting
description:
About the Team
The DoorDash Lease Accounting team ensures DoorDash’s lease portfolio is reported accurately and on time under ASC 842. This requires deep technical accounting review and careful interpretation of complex, often ambiguous lease arrangements. As the portfolio grows in size and complexity, we continue to strengthen our processes to keep pace with the business.
About the Role
You will report to the Senior Accounting Manager on our Lease Accounting team. As the Lease Accounting Manager, you will be a key technical expert on ASC 842, ensuring DoorDash’s leases are accounted for accurately as the business grows. This role is built for someone who takes ownership, stays ahead of the work, and works closely with partners across functions. Success means well-supported conclusions and dependable reporting each period, with the opportunity to apply your expertise to increasingly complex leases.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Review lease abstractions against new lease agreements and lease modifications to ensure accurate classification and recognition of each lease in accordance with ASC 842.
Perform detailed accounting analysis of complex lease arrangements and unique scenarios that go beyond standard treatment, documenting conclusions and supporting analysis.
Perform lease monthly close activities including journal entries, account reconciliations, and flux analysis
Own lease financial reporting deliverables, including cash flows, rollforwards, and disclosures.
Partner closely with Real Estate, Lease Administration and other cross-functional teams to understand lease activity early and keep the accounting accurate and timely.
Proactively identify and lead process improvements and automation initiatives to reduce manual work and improve the accuracy and efficiency of processes.
Maintain lease SOX controls and support both internal and external audit requests.
We’re excited about you because…
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, or a related field, and/or equivalent work experience.
6+ years accounting experience, including in-depth experience applying US GAAP lease accounting (ASC 842), which is essential to this role.
Proven experience reviewing lease agreements, interpreting lease terms, and assessing their financial implications to determine the appropriate accounting treatment.
Ownership mindset and proactiveness, with a track record of managing multiple deliverables and following them through to completion on close timelines.
Strong cross-functional partnership and communication skills to work effectively with internal and external partners.
Close attention to detail and demonstrated problem-solving skills.

description:
About the Team
The Identity and Access Management (IAM) team enables secure, seamless access across DoorDash's global engineering and business operations. Our mission is to make access simple, automated, and user-centric, reducing friction through self-service solutions while maintaining strong governance and compliance. We focus on streamlining identity lifecycle processes, modernising access governance, and building scalable controls that enable employees and engineers to work efficiently and securely.
About the Role
We are looking for a hands-on IAM leader who can turn strategy into tangible outcomes, combining technical implementation, control ownership, and team leadership. Operating with a global remit, you will partner closely with the UK-based Global Head of IAM to execute our strategy, while leading delivery, resolving operational challenges, and supporting stakeholders across US time zones and the wider business. This requires flexibility to work earlier hours to maximise collaboration with the UK, while maintaining sufficient coverage across US teams. Within your first 60 days, we expect you to have independently delivered measurable improvements in access governance, audit remediation, lifecycle controls, or automation, before taking on responsibility for managing and growing our US IAM engineering team following an initial onboarding period.
You will report into the Global Head of Identity and Access Management on our Identity and Access Management team in our Security organisation.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will…
Build solutions, not just designs: Architect, configure, and implement IAM improvements using identity platforms, APIs, scripting, and automation, delivering minimum viable solutions quickly while progressing toward scalable strategic designs.

Lead IAM delivery in the US: Independently prioritise and resolve operational challenges, make risk-informed decisions, deliver against global IAM objectives, and build and develop a high-performing engineering team.
Create compliance by design: Build agile, automated IAM solutions that meet security and audit requirements by default, embedding effective controls into everyday workflows rather than relying on manual checks and retrospective remediation.
Shape the future of identity: Advance role-based and attribute-based access models, while exploring emerging opportunities in non-human identity and AI agent governance.
We're excited about you because…
You have 8+ years of IAM experience, including direct, hands-on ownership of user access reviews, identity lifecycle controls, SoX audit evidence, and remediation of control deficiencies.

title: Product Marketing Manager Platform & Technology
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
Impact In This Role
In this role, you’ll own the positioning, messaging, and go-to-market strategy for our unified platform that brings standard, configurable, and custom mechanical components together under one sourcing experience.
What You’ll Be Doing
Owning platform positioning and messaging — articulating why a unified platform across standard, configurable, and custom components matters, and how AI-driven quoting, automated DFM, and global manufacturing capacity come together as a single value proposition
Partnering closely with Product Management and Engineering to shape product messaging, positioning, and competitive strategy, and to feed customer and market insight back into roadmap decisions
Championing an AI-driven mindset — helping identify and articulate where AI can enhance the applications and solutions we deliver to customers, and translating those capabilities into clear market-facing value
Developing clear, effective messaging by persona and industry vertical — including machine builders, mechanical engineers, and supply chain/procurement leaders — for use in marketing and sales campaigns
Maintaining up-to-date messaging and product marketing assets across the platform and technology stack
Interacting with customers and sales reps to document win/loss analysis and deepen our understanding of our target audience
Evaluating MISUMI Americas positioning against the competition — including both distribution-model players and digital manufacturing competitors — to sharpen differentiation in the market
Directing launch campaigns for new platform capabilities and technology releases
Partnering with Product Marketing and Marketing teams to build world-class content, sales tools, and other digital assets — emails, ads, web landing pages, brochures, and technical positioning — that build pipeline and drive bookings
Enabling our sales teams with product trainings and sales enablement materials
Identifying case studies and testimonials that provide clear, quantifiable examples of the platform’s value
Desired Traits
7-10 years of experience in manufacturing/supply chain technology, sales, and/or product marketing roles, ideally including technical or platform products
B.S. in engineering or B.A. in business, marketing, or other relevant field
An AI-driven mindset — you’re comfortable thinking about how AI can enhance the applications and solutions we deliver to customers, and you can translate that thinking into product positioning and go-to-market strategy
Proven experience marketing SaaS products or software applications — you understand platform-based business models, release cycles, and how to position software value to both technical and business buyers
Direct experience with manufacturing and/or supply chain technology systems (e.g., ERP, MES, PLM, procurement/sourcing platforms, or similar systems) — you understand how these systems fit into a customer’s broader technology stack and workflow
Hands-on manufacturing experience or a strong working knowledge of manufacturing processes (e.g., CNC machining, injection molding, sheet metal, 3D printing) and how they map to engineering and sourcing decisions
You are a strategic thinker, able to translate complex technical capability into clear, focused messaging and actions
You are an excellent writer, comfortable developing blogs, brochures, and landing page copy
You are highly organized and a strong project manager, able to keep multiple stakeholders — Product, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing — on track toward a launch deadline
Comfortable working in a matrix-driven model across a company integrating two organizations and scaling a platform in real time
Experience marketing to a span of personas, from technical and operational audiences (e.g., mechanical engineers, machine builders) to senior-level executives (e.g., manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, operations)

Ability to travel 25% annually in North America for team meetings, customer meetings, offsites, trade shows, conferences, supplier partner meetings.

Location: San Francisco Bay Area, CA (Remote — Bay Area Only)

Build the Manufacturing Network Behind the World’s Best Hardware
Fictiv is building the world’s leading platform for hardware manufacturing—and our supplier network is at the heart of that mission.
As a Senior Strategic Sourcing Specialist , you’ll be responsible for building, qualifying, and strengthening Fictiv’s U.S.-based manufacturing partner network . You’ll work hands-on with CNC, sheet metal, additive manufacturing, and injection molding suppliers to ensure we have the right capabilities, capacity, quality, and cost structure to support our customers at scale.
This is a remote role , but candidates must live in the San Francisco Bay Area . Local presence is essential, as this position involves frequent, in-person visits to manufacturing partners to assess capabilities, develop relationships, and drive continuous improvement.
This is not a transactional sourcing role and not a desk-only job. You’ll spend time on factory floors, in production discussions, and working directly with suppliers to solve real manufacturing challenges.
You’ll report to the Manager of Strategic Sourcing, U.S. , and serve as a senior individual contributor and subject-matter expert within the Strategic Sourcing team.

Manufacturing partner performance
Customer satisfaction and repeat business
Fictiv’s ability to scale complex manufacturing programs
Cost, lead time, and operational resilience across the U.S. supply base
You’ll ensure Fictiv maintains a balanced, high-performing domestic supplier network —one that can meet demanding technical requirements while staying competitive on cost and lead time.
This role requires ongoing engagement with suppliers , both virtually and on-site, to evaluate performance, resolve issues, and drive long-term improvements.

Identify, evaluate, and onboard new U.S.-based manufacturing partners
Conduct on-site assessments of technical capability, capacity, and operational readiness
Ensure suppliers align with Fictiv’s standards, goals, and long-term strategy

Partner with Quality, Operations, and Engineering to address performance gaps

Drive consistent supplier engagement and adherence to Fictiv standards and expectations
Optimize Cost, Capacity & Network Health
Manage a strategically balanced domestic supplier portfolio
Optimize spend allocation, capacity utilization, and capability coverage
Analyze cost structures, utilization data, and performance metrics to drive efficiency and transparency
Collaborate Across the Business
Partner closely with Sales, Product Management, Quality, Costing/DFM, and Operations teams
Align supplier strategies with customer needs and program requirements
Support supply chain development for large or complex customer programs
Be Present on the Factory Floor
Conduct regular on-site visits to manufacturing partner facilities
Assess real-world production constraints and opportunities
Strengthen partnerships through direct, face-to-face collaboration

Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills

Strong project management capability

title: Account Executive, Flexport Capital
description:
About Flexport:
At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
Account Executive, Flexport Capital
Flexport helps more than 10,000 clients and suppliers lead all aspects of their supply chain operations. Each of these customers faces significant working capital burdens that hamper their ability to grow their businesses. Since inception, Flexport Capital has provided over $2 billion in loans to Flexport customers to address these needs. Our non-dilutive capital products empower businesses to grow and bridge their working capital needs while maintaining ownership and control. As a start-up within a start-up, we’re developing unique fintech products that leverage the resources and data of Flexport’s platform for global trade. We are seeking an entrepreneurial and financially savvy individual to join our tight-knit team.
The Opportunity: Flexport Capital is Flexport’s financing arm, offering inventory and logistics financing, asset-based lending, term loans, and working capital products to Flexport clients. As an Account Executive, you will own the full end-to-end sales cycle for Flexport Capital, from sourcing, prospecting, negotiation, underwriting coordination, and close. You will build and manage your own growing book of business. You will serve as the primary commercial voice for your customers, acting as a financial consultant and strategic advisor to founders, CFOs, and finance teams seeking working capital solutions. You will work directly with Credit, Product, and Legal as a peer partner, shaping product development and go-to-market strategy based on real market feedback. You’ll play a critical role in scaling Flexport Capital’s market presence and establishing it as the go-to financing partner for growth stage businesses. You’ll own building the sales playbook that drives this growth, with full autonomy over your territory and clear upside as you scale.
You Will:
Own the full end-to-end sales cycle for your territory, from sourcing and prospecting through deal structuring, underwriting coordination, closing, and early relationship management.
Build and own a growing book of business with direct revenue accountability. You'll win new customers, expand relationships as they scale, and identify cross-sell opportunities within your territory.
Serve as the commercial relationship owner for your clients. You'll negotiate terms, structure deals, and coordinate with Credit through underwriting to close.
Use Flexport's supply chain data as a commercial advantage . By analyzing shipment patterns, volume spikes, transit times, and invoice data, you can identify when customers need capital and turn those signals into targeted actions to drive sustainable growth.
Drive strategic initiatives related to growth strategy, sales motions, and capital markets partnerships that expand Flexport Capital's market position.
Leverage Flexport's freight and omni capabilities to create working capital solutions that deepen customer relationships, increase wallet share, and win deals competitors can't.
You Should Have:
Experience - 6+ years of experience in sales/sales development for a financial services and/or a technology company. Previous startup experience is a plus.
Financial & Credit Acumen - Fluency in working capital structures, financial statement analysis, and lending mechanics. You can read and interpret P&Ls, balance sheets, and cash flow statements to assess customer needs. You'll be expected to recommend appropriate lending structures and create tailored working capital solutions for each prospect based on their business model and financing needs.
Full-cycle sales execution - You’ve owned deals from prospect through close. You understand pipeline management, deal structuring, and how to navigate complex sales cycles. You’ve hit and exceeded quota consistently.
Communication & Presence - Excellent communication and executive presence. You can build trusted relationships with Founders, CEOs, CFOs, and Finance Directors. You navigate senior-level conversations with ease and represent your company credibly with C-suite buyers.
Commercial drive and ownership - You’re motivated by building and growing a business. You think like an owner, take accountability for outcomes, and proactively solve problems to move deals forward.
Strategic business sense - You see beyond individual deals. You understand market trends, competitive threats, and identify customer needs that create product/GTM opportunities.
Data & Tools - Proficiency in Salesforce, Excel, Claude, and other data tools. Ability to design dashboards and reporting frameworks to track pipeline growth and buying signals.

description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
Ready for a new adventure? Build your career at the forefront of robotics and industrial automation while exploring the country! Bring your technical skills, curiosity, and sense of adventure. We'll bring the robots, the challenges, and the opportunity to explore somewhere new.
As Formic's customer base and robot fleet expand nationwide, we're looking for talented, adventurous Robotics Field Service Engineers (FSEs) and Field Service Technicians (FSTs) who are excited to go wherever opportunity takes them. We'll help you relocate to a market where your skills are needed, with the possibility of moving again as our fleet grows and new opportunities emerge. Whether you're an experienced technician ready for bigger challenges or an accomplished engineer looking for your next chapter, you'll work with cutting-edge robotics, solve meaningful technical problems, and help transform manufacturing across America.

Establish a disciplined operating cadence that translates performance insights into decisions about strategy, priorities, budget, and resources, holding the organization accountable for outcomes rather than activity.

Translate broad company objectives into clear priorities, ownership, expectations, and measurable outcomes that connect the team's work to business goals.
Make disciplined decisions about priorities and resources, challenging assumptions, stopping initiatives that aren't delivering results, and adapting as we learn.
Stay close enough to the work to identify problems early, remove obstacles, and hold people accountable without becoming a bottleneck to execution.
Foster a culture of transparency, constructive challenge, and open communication about performance, priorities, tradeoffs, and lessons learned.
Establish accountability for external agencies, contractors, and technology partners, including deliverables, performance, costs, documentation, and continuity, while building sustainable processes that preserve institutional knowledge and support organizational change.

Lead and align af multidisciplinary organization spanning Marketing, content and creative, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering around shared commercial goals.
Build a high-performing team by establishing clear expectations, delegating meaningful ownership, coaching and developing talent, and addressing performance gaps directly.

The Strategic Sourcing Manager develops and executes sourcing strategies that support business objectives related to cost, quality, delivery, innovation, and supplier performance for both the Hatfield Industrial and Tech business units (SIMHD). Develop contingency sourcing strategies to ensure supply continuity and minimize operational disruptions.

The intern will get hands-on experience with software development, data management, machine learning, and systems design thinking. Beyond technical skills, this internship will require effective communication with numerous cross-functional stakeholders.

Assist in integrating additional large language model (LLM) workflows into this system.
Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to develop the solution.
Present and interpret findings to a broad range of teams across the organization.

Self-motivated individual with a strong interest in data science and machine learning.

Intuitive Accessories are the interface between all aspects of the da Vinci system and enable safe and effective robot-assisted surgery. Our customers interact directly with Accessories in every surgical procedure, and they serve a critical role in customer satisfaction and patient outcomes.
The Mechanical Engineer, Product Engineering for Single-Port Accessories will provide engineering support across the product portfolio. Projects will include a mix of product improvements for cost savings and manufacturability to enable significant volume growth, along with enhancements to improve reliability and usability. The successful candidate will thrive in a fast-paced environment, have a passion for continuous improvement, and possess the ability to bring cross-functional teams together to solve problems.  A strong sense of responsibility and ownership is required, as well as a commitment to high quality.

Review and define functional requirements based on user and product-level requirements and international standards, and maintain Design History Files per regulatory and corporate requirements

Create and maintain product specifications (including engineering drawings) with careful consideration for critical functions and safety while designing for manufacturability and cost, in accordance with corporate operating procedures
Troubleshoot issues and get to root cause quickly using thorough and logical methods
Iterate design solutions rapidly by prototyping, testing, and analyzing using engineering principles and techniques, including computer simulation and physical models

Collaborate with manufacturing and supplier engineering to facilitate transfer of designs into sustainable production
Establish individual goals aligned with overall project and company goals.

Passion for continuous improvement and a commitment to quality
Understanding concepts of design input, design output, requirement traceability, and FMEA risk analysis
Mechanical analysis, including statics, dynamics, and strength of materials
Demonstrated ability to design for reliability and manufacturability
Exposure to full product development lifecycle including ideation, design, analysis, debug, verification, qualification, transfer to manufacturing, and sustaining

Experience designing plastic components and assemblies

Proficiency at failure analysis, including root cause analysis techniques (e.g., fishbone, 5 Whys, etc.)

Comfortable operating machine shop, measurement, and test equipment

Ability to communicate effectively (written and verbal) across functions, including presenting to a technical audience

Sense of shared responsibility and reward
Ability to excel in a fast-paced, high transaction, mass-production environment
Ability to utilize deep technical knowledge and broad expertise to achieve company objectives in creative and effective ways
Experience leading cross-functional meetings
Knowledge of sterilization methods, biocompatibility, and packaging of medical devices
Knowledge of additional manufacturing processes such as extrusion, blow molding, ultrasonic welding, RF welding, heat staking, and laser welding
Prior experience working in a regulated industry (medical device strongly preferred)

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Taxation, or a related field

CPA or Master’s in Taxation preferred.

Willingness to leverage AI tools and emerging technologies required, previous experience preferred.
