This role is responsible for establishing policies guiding strategies and execution of planning tools, processes, and personnel to direct planning activities at raw component level. Responsibilities cover component yield planning, lineside kanban sizing, ensuring the accuracy of MRP Plan loads, ECO process guidance/best practices, component planning /E&O mitigation strategies for major product transitions and chronic shortage analysis. The position collaborates with Planning, Procurement, Manufacturing and Service teams to streamline component planning/ material flow and drive processes for operational excellence, including recovery plan for chronic shortages, component flow from warehouse to the lines.
Essential Job Duties
·         Understand top level Finished good and subassembly demand and be able to communicate demand changes at the component level. Directly responsible for MRP integrity at the component level along with understanding component buffering, inventory strategies and E&O analysis and root cause.
Responsible for the component level yield planning review and material load process, by collaborating closely with procurement teams by sharing historical trends, forward planning and scrap reduction opportunities.
Lead the Line Side Kanban Sizing & the closed loop implementation of recommended sizing by collaborating with Manufacturing, Warehouse and Inventory Control teams.
·         Works with Production Planning and Manufacturing functions to identify chronic shortages and works with Procurement teams on critical priorities/recovery and improve material flow processes from warehouse to the Manufacturing lines.
Manages material flow between factories, including transfers, and allocation of raw materials across production lines, warehouses, and factory locations.
·         Works with planning and procurement teams on major product transitions, to minimize raw material E&O, through effective communication, sharing best practices, leading impact assessment/ mitigation actions. Supervises the Alternate parts planning process to ensure data integrity of raw components.
Drive periodic review/ clean-up actions for NPI planning material in the NPI locations
Establish key performance metrics, facilitate enhancement of planning tools and ERP/MRP system functionality for scalable raw material planning and MRP integrity.
Rigor in operational excellence, projects and initiatives to drive business outcomes.
Required Skills and Experience
·         Detailed understanding of material planning, demand scheduling, and supply planning with strong knowledge of ERP systems and advanced planning systems.
·         Strong process driven mindset, data/analytical capabilities, ability to solve problems and drive future system and process solutions.
·         Key abilities include conflict resolution, consensus building, and gaining commitment of stakeholders to achieve results.
·         Demonstrated skill in influencing cross-functional colleagues within a matrixed and multinational environment to accomplish objectives and promote best practices for systems tools, processes, and planning competencies.
·         Excellent verbal, written, presentation, executive communication skills and the ability to interact professionally with a diverse group of internal customers.
Required Education and Training
·         Masters or BS degree or equivalent.
·         12+ years of experience in Production Planning, Demand/Supply planning, Purchasing, Inventory Management domains
·         5+ years of experience in directly managing high performing teams.
·         Multi-plant work experience highly desired
Working Conditions
~20% travel to both domestic and international operating sites.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience working in medium to large medical device manufacturing organizations within multinational and cross-matrixed management settings.
Masters level degree in engineering, supply chain/business management, finance discipline.
·         Significant experience with core business systems including SAP, Agile, advanced planning solutions

They are responsible for developing the surgical teleoperation, motion control, and safety algorithms. This responsibility crosses into electrical, mechanical, software, control, user interface, and safety engineering. Apply control theory to the design and verification of mechatronic and tele-robotic systems.

Develop and implement motion control and safety algorithms, including documentation of risks, requirements, and test protocols.

Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic.
Communicate system performance to the organization.
Support and track system performance as it evolves from design engineering to manufacturing.
Provide analytical assistance and tool building for other engineering issues.

Document and communicate intellectual property.

Minimum MS degree in CS, ME, EE, or similar with 4–5+ years of industrial experience or PhD with 1–3+ years of experience.
Experience designing and implementing servo control systems.
Possess strong embedded development skills including intimate knowledge of C and modern C++.
Possess MATLAB and Python programming capabilities, as well as hardware and software integration skills.
Be detail-oriented and able to develop and drive a single solution to completion.
Comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis.
Hands-on engineering experience with proven ability to work well in a team environment.
Self-motivated and proactive in engaging with interdisciplinary teams to address and solve complex problems.
A desire to deliver a quality and innovative product that will improve millions of people’s lives!

Primary Function of Position:
The Staff Software Engineer will lead the design and evolution of a modern, scalable Data-as-a-Service (DaaS) platform that supports Intuitive Digital products and enables more than 2,000 engineers across the organization. This role is responsible for owning and advancing critical components of our real-time and micro-batch data pipelines that power product development, internal tools, and analytics. The engineer will provide architectural direction, influence cross-team data standards, ensure reliability and performance at scale, and drive strategic initiatives that improve developer productivity and data accessibility across the organization.
Major work will focus on enabling high-throughput, low-latency data delivery through streaming pipelines, dynamic transformations, and APIs, driving application development, AI/ML, and actionable insights. Build highly scalable distributed systems that leverage event-based and streaming data pipelines to handle ingestion and processing of robot, manufacturing, and clinical data
Enable users by providing self-service APIs and applications to access and interact with data
Work closely with core engineering teams to consistently evolve data models based on growing business needs
Apply and evangelize software development best practices such as CI/CD, automated testing, infrastructure-as-code, and microservice architectures

Fluent coding with at least two of the following: Python, Go, Scala, Java, C++

Primary Function of Position
The Staff Supplier Quality Engineer operates with a high degree of independence to determine methodologies, audit frameworks, quality systems, and procedural controls across the global supply chain ecosystem, reporting to the Director, Global Supply Chain Audits.
This role is responsible for the technical execution, continuous improvement, strategic projects, and global harmonization of Third-Party Logistics (3PL) quality management, distribution center controls, and service supplier qualification processes worldwide. The Staff SQE leads risk-based lead audit programs, ensures conformance to applicable global regulatory standards (21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485, EU MDR 2017/745, Good Distribution Practice / GDP), and serves as a subject matter expert (SME) in regulatory body inspections. S/he partners with cross-functional global operations, logistics, and regional RAQA organizations to drive critical process improvement projects, resolve systemic quality issues, ensure CAPA effectiveness, and advance 3PL supply chain compliance maturity.
Essential Job Duties
·         3PL Quality Management & Worldwide Oversight
·         Design, own, and continuously improve a global 3PL Quality Management Program encompassing third-party logistics providers, global distribution hubs, forward stocking locations, cold chain/temperature-controlled storage facilities, and fulfillment partners across all global regions.
·         Establish and maintain qualification frameworks, quality agreements (QAs), and re-evaluation controls specific to 3PL providers and logistics vendors supporting GxP-regulated distribution processes in alignment with 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485 (Clause 7.5.5), EU MDR, and GDP requirements.

·         Conduct Lead Audits against applicable global regulatory standards including Good Distribution Practice (GDP), ISO 13485, ISO 17025, ISO 11135/11137, and 21 CFR Part 820 subpart requirements.
·         Evaluate audit findings, issue formal audit reports, drive root cause analysis rigor with 3PL leadership, and manage SCAR / CAPA phase gate reviews and effectiveness verifications.
·         Projects & Process Improvements
·         Lead strategic quality engineering projects and continuous process improvement initiatives to optimize supply chain workflows, streamline 3PL quality oversight, and elevate supplier scorecards.

·         Own Process Nonconformances (NCs) and CAPAs related to 3PL, logistics, and supply chain audit processes, ensuring root cause rigor (6M / 5-Why) and sustainable corrective actions.
·         Supplier Controls & QMS Administration
·         Manage 3PL Supplier Corrective Action Requests (SCARs) end-to-end: issuance, aging tracking, phase gate reviews, effectiveness verification, and closure.
·         Support Approved Supplier List (ASL) governance regarding 3PL status maintenance, including promotions, conditional approvals, and demotions.
·         Administer and maintain 3PL and service supplier records in Trackwise, SAP, and Agile, including audit files, ISO/GDP certifications, quality agreements, and ARFs.
·         Regulatory Audit Support & Leadership
·         Serve as SME during FDA inspections, Notified Body audits (e.g., BSI, TÜV), and internal QMS audits for all matters related to 3PL Controls, GDP compliance, Service Supplier qualification, and Supply Chain Audits.
·         Operate independently to determine methods and procedures on new, complex, or special assignments with minimal supervision.
·         Mentor, coach, and guide junior compliance and supplier quality engineering staff.
·         May supervise or mentor the activities of junior compliance and supplier quality staff.
Required Skills and Experience
ISO 13485 Lead Auditor with demonstrated experience leading multi-site external audits worldwide.
Expert-level knowledge of 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485:2016, EU MDR 2017/745, and Good Distribution Practice (GDP / GMP) requirements applicable to 3PL, logistics, and service supplier controls.
Proven experience leading quality oversight and audits of global 3PLs, cold chain storage, distribution networks, and service suppliers.
Expert proficiency with QMS platforms including Trackwise, SAP, and Agile for supplier file management, SCAR tracking, and audit scheduling.
Strong understanding of risk management principles (ISO 14971) as applied to 3PL risk stratification, logistics risk assessments, and audit frequency determination.

description:
Job Purpose
To ensure we are supplying customers with the highest quality products while adhering to all food and safety standards. This is accomplished by batching food product/condiments to corporate/customer approved recipes.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
• Obtains instruction from lead processor or supervisor.
• Ability to follow complete production schedules with minimal scrap/spoilage
• Keep up with volume of work required
• Visually inspects equipment at station for cleanliness or obvious maintenance problems.
• Cleans small machine components, as needed.
• Reports any problems to lead processor or supervisor.
• Makes piping connections as needed for particular process on schedule.
• Monitors equipment controls, temperature meters, valves and adjusts as needed.
• Operates forklift/pallet jack to obtain ingredients or move pallets/totes in and around processing area.
• While slow, assists processing assistants in cleaning processing areas by scrubbing walls, hosing floor, sweeping floor/emptying trash and performing other cleaning duties.
• Utilizes can openers, knives, band cutters, snips, pliers and other small items to open ingredient cases/packages.
• Maintains neat work area. Wipes spills that have occurred during mixing process.
• Records data pertaining to work completed, ingredients used, lot codes and other processing information.
• Assists in cleaning equipment and lines between recipes.
• Very occasionally obtains ingredients/supplies from warehouse.
• Obtains samples of batches and taste test.
• Asks lead, supervisor or material handler if there is any rework.
• Uses rework if there is any consistently.
• Determines ingredients required for formula/recipe and the required amount.
• Ability to safely lift 50lbs on a regular basis.
• Obtains ingredients from storage area or around work area and pours into kettle.
• Meters in other ingredients as required by watching meters and turning on/off kettle.
• Utilizes drum lift by strapping drum into lift and operating hydraulic lift with chain.
• Manually pushes drum lift to kettle and dumps drum of ingredients as needed.
• Operates controls to activate mixers and equipment.
• Monitors controls, equipment temperature, valves, and adjusts equipment to meet formula requirements.
• Hoses spills off floor and hoses towards drains.
• Obtains, measures and weighs additional ingredients to set aside in preparation for next batch or recipe.
• Assists other processors in pouring ingredients into kettles as needed.
• Collects samples and tests for pH, acidity, viscosity and solids.
• Reads test results and adjusts equipment/recipe accordingly.
• Notifies lead processor of any major adjustments needed, or problems with process.
• Transfers finished products to drum, tote, or tank by pumping through piping system.
• Operates switches to control pumps when batch is complete.
• Assists in preparing drums, totes, or tanks for storage of product by ensuring that the proper placarding information is on the package.
• Determines appropriate size of batch needed to accommodate orders and line.
• Closely monitors batch temperature while processing and waiting for packaging to ensure that product will not set prematurely.
• Operates equipment in a safe manner following GMP guidelines and keeps work area clean.
• Supports the Jacksonville plant FSQ and QRMP initiatives on any and all procedures/programs pertaining to product safety.
• Participates in meetings and have scheduling flexibility.
• Trains others as necessary.
• Fills in for other positions as necessary.
• Occasionally testing batches in the lab and recording information on proper documentation.
• Additional responsibilities of this position include assisting in the creation of a culture of safety and health by performing work safely in accordance with all company safety procedures.
• Operates equipment safely and reports any unsafe work conditions or practice to supervisor. Occupational safety and health performance is measured in this position
• Other duties as assigned

Join Our Greenies Team in North Kansas City
At Mars Petcare, we are passionate about pets. Our Greenies brand is dedicated to keeping pets healthy and happy, and we manufacture our world-renowned products right here in our highly desirable, fully climate-controlled North Kansas City facility.
Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity. The opportunity to do the kind of challenging, interesting work that shapes the world’s best-loved brands. To work with real purpose, supported by talented, friendly people from all sorts of different backgrounds.
Whether you are an experienced warehouse professional, a skilled forklift operator looking for a stable day-shift position, or a transitioning military Veteran, Reservist, or National Guard member, we welcome your unique talents! We highly value the dedication, safety-first mindset, and structured teamwork developed in the military and look forward to helping you build a successful civilian career.
Job Summary
The Material Handler is responsible for the end-to-end logistics flow within our plant. This dual-focus role handles all incoming packaging and raw ingredients, manages safe product movement inside the site, loads outbound trailers for shipment, completes all logistics paperwork, and maintains perfect inventory control. This associate works closely with production, purchasing, receiving, shipping, and quality teams to ensure seamless plant operations in a clean, temperature-controlled environment.
Key Responsibilities
Receiving & Inbound Logistics
Receive and verify all incoming raw materials, ingredients, packaging, and components against purchase orders and shipping manifests.
Use a forklift to safely unload inbound trucks and transfer materials to their correct designated storage locations.
Conduct strict quality and food safety checks on incoming materials, including collecting product samples and verifying supplier paperwork.
Collaborate with external logistics departments and freight carriers to ensure correct and safe delivery of production materials.
Material Handling & Warehouse Operations
Safely and accurately operate material handling equipment (including forklifts) to transport inventory, raw materials, WIP (work-in-process), and finished goods throughout the facility.
Support production schedules by ensuring that the correct materials are issued and staged in production areas when needed.
Stage, build, and load outbound trailers for shipment, ensuring proper cargo weight distribution and trailer utilization.
Ensure proper labeling, sorting, FIFO (First-In, First-Out) rotation, and general organization of all materials in storage areas.
Inventory, Systems, & Documentation
Scan and track material movements using warehouse management systems to ensure perfect real-time inventory accountability.
Perform daily cycle counts, participate in precision monthly inventories, and assist with formal physical audits.
Investigate inventory discrepancies promptly and report findings to management.
Generate, review, and complete accurate shipping/receiving paperwork, logging all transactions accurately into the plant database.
Safety, Quality, & Food Safety Culture
Participate and adhere to all food safety requirements, Quality Management Processes (QMPs), and site safety programs, championing a safety-first culture.
Maintain a clean, organized, and sanitary warehouse environment in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
Promptly report any safety, food safety, or quality concerns to leadership.
Position Requirements
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent civilian/military education.
Experience: Proven experience in warehouse logistics, receiving, shipping, or material handling roles.
Equipment: Demonstrated experience operating a forklift safely in an industrial or warehouse environment.
Physical Ability: Must be in good physical condition with the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, bend, reach, climb, and safely lift up to 40 pounds manually.
Technical Literacy: Working knowledge of basic computer programs for entering data, record keeping, and maintaining inventory logs.
Core Skills: Basic math skills, a keen eye for detail, strong organizational skills, and excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Teamwork: Demonstrated ability to work in a high-performing team environment with a willingness to learn and be coached.
Military & Veteran Technical Equivalency Guide
At Mars, we recognize that your military service has prepared you to excel in logistical operations. Your training in high-stakes material movement, precision inventory tracking, and supply chain management maps directly to this role. If you served in any of the following specialties, we highly encourage you to apply:
U.S. Army: Automated Logistical Specialist (92A), Unit Supply Specialist (92Y), Cargo Specialist (88H), Motor Transport Operator (88M), Ammunition Specialist (89B). Your experience with warehouse databases, material handling equipment (MHE), and precise property book audits is an excellent fit.
U.S. Navy: Logistics Specialist (LS), Storekeeper, Aviation Storekeeper (AK). Your experience managing inventory, shipboard supply warehouses, and processing shipping manifests maps directly to our material tracking systems.
U.S. Air Force: Materiel Management (2S0X1), Traffic Management (2T0X1), Ground Transportation (2T1X1). Your training in cargo loading, receiving inspections, strict compliance with safety procedures, and inventory precision is an exact match.
U.S. Marine Corps: Warehouse Clerk (3051), Supply Administration & Operations (3043), Logistics/Embarkation Specialist (0431), Motor Vehicle Operator (3531). Your focus on cargo staging, load planning, and material handling equipment matches our shipping and receiving operations.
U.S. Coast Guard: Storekeeper (SK), Marine Science Technician.
What We Offer (Total Rewards & Benefits)
At Mars, being an associate is more than a job—it's an opportunity to build a long-term career. We provide a competitive, industry-leading package starting on your very first day:
Compensation: Competitive base pay based on experience, shift differentials, and significant overtime (OT) potential.
Annual Bonus: Eligibility for our annual performance-based company bonus and annual merit increases.
Health & Wellness: Comprehensive Medical, Vision, and Dental insurance starting on Day One.
Retirement Planning: An exceptional 401(k) program with up to 6% company match.
Work-Life Balance: Generous paid vacation time, paid holidays, and predictable rotating 2-2-3 day shifts.
Family Support: Paid Parental Leave, plus Short-Term and Long-Term Disability.
Career Growth: Access to top-tier learning and development through Mars University.
Onsite Perks: Access to our onsite gym.
About Mars, Incorporated
Mars is a family-owned business with over a century of history making diverse products and offering services for people and the pets people love. We produce some of the world’s best-loved brands: M&M’s®, SNICKERS®, TWIX®, MILKY WAY®, DOVE®, PEDIGREE®, ROYAL CANIN®, WHISKAS®, EXTRA®, ORBIT®, 5™, SKITTLES®, BEN’S ORIGINAL®, and COCOAVIA®.
Alongside our consumer brands, we proudly take care of half of the world’s pets through our nutrition, health, and services businesses such as Banfield Pet Hospitals™, BluePearl®, Linnaeus, AniCura, VCA™, and Pet Partners™.
The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency, and Freedom – inspire our 130,000 Associates to take action every day toward creating the world we want tomorrow.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Controllership team delivers the financial truth that powers OpenAI’s growth. By translating operational activity into accurate, timely, and decision-grade financial data, we enable leadership to scale the business with confidence. Our commitment to rigorous controls and best-in-class systems ensures financial integrity as OpenAI grows. 

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a strategic and execution-oriented Accounting Lead, Hardware to build and scale inventory accounting capabilities across consumer hardware and robotics businesses. This role partners closely with Finance, Supply Chain, Manufacturing Operations, Technical Accounting, Strategic Finance, and Systems teams to establish scalable inventory and supply chain accounting processes and reporting infrastructure supporting rapid growth and product launches.

The ideal candidate brings strong accounting fundamentals, sound judgment, and a track record of building scalable processes in complex, evolving businesses. Inventory, cost accounting, or supply chain experience is preferred, and accounting experience supporting hardware, infrastructure, data centers, or other capital-intensive operations is also valuable. We welcome strong accounting professionals from other backgrounds who have demonstrated the ability to quickly learn unfamiliar business models and accounting topics and take ownership of new areas. This person should thrive in ambiguity, combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution, and communicate effectively with cross-functional partners and senior leadership.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: 


INVENTORY ACCOUNTING

 - Lead inventory and supply chain accounting across consumer hardware and robotics programs, including inventory valuation, supply chain/sourcing arrangements, manufacturing variances, reserves, and close processes.

 - Partner with Supply Chain, Operations, and Strategic Finance to support BOM accuracy, labor and overhead assumptions, operationalize supply chain strategies and gross margin analysis.

 - Develop scalable accounting processes for NPI, prototyping, engineering builds, and mass production.

 - Own inventory-related accounting policies and controls, including capitalization, overhead allocation, LCNRV/NRV assessments, rebates, freight, tariffs, and inventory controls.


ERP SYSTEMS & PROCESS DESIGN

 - Serve as a finance lead for Oracle Fusion manufacturing costing and inventory implementations, enhancements, and process optimization.

 - Partner with Systems, IT, and Operations to design scalable finance processes, controls, reporting structures, and operational workflows.

 - Partner with Systems and Operations to define accounting requirements and guide ERP design for product costing, inventory transactions, and related reporting and controls.


FINANCIAL CLOSE, REPORTING & CONTROLS

 - Lead monthly, quarterly, and annual cost accounting close activities and improve scalable reconciliations, reporting, and management review processes.

 - Partner with Strategic Finance on margin reporting, inventory analytics, and budget versus actual analysis.

 - Establish SOX-ready controls, support audits and technical accounting matters, and drive continuous improvement across close and reporting processes.


CROSS-FUNCTIONAL LEADERSHIP

 - Act as a strategic partner to Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Program Management teams.

 - Translate ambiguous business needs into scalable accounting and operational frameworks.

 - Influence senior stakeholders through strong communication, executive presence, and data-driven recommendations.

 - Help build and scale the long-term roadmap for hardware controllership, manufacturing accounting, and operational finance infrastructure.

 


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Bring strong accounting judgment and enjoy learning how physical products, infrastructure, and operational workflows translate into financial reporting.

 - Have a track record of quickly developing expertise in unfamiliar accounting areas, asking thoughtful questions, and turning what you learn into practical processes and controls.

 - Can comfortably operate between strategic leadership discussions and highly detailed operational accounting analyses.

 - Have strong executive presence and can communicate effectively with senior leadership and cross-functional partners.

 - Enjoy building scalable processes and infrastructure in fast-moving, ambiguous environments.

 - Are highly detail-oriented and maintain a strong control mindset while balancing business partnership.

 - Have a strong systems orientation and enjoy designing scalable ERP and reporting processes.

 - Are intellectually curious, proactive, and solutions-oriented.

 


QUALIFICATIONS


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

 - 8+ years of progressive accounting experience, with ownership of complex accounting areas, close processes, or operational accounting.

 - Strong understanding of U.S. GAAP and demonstrated ability to research unfamiliar accounting topics and apply sound judgment.

 - Demonstrated ability to quickly learn new business models, systems, and operational processes and take ownership of unfamiliar accounting areas.

 - Experience building or improving accounting processes, reconciliations, controls, and reporting.

 - Strong systems aptitude and experience working with ERP systems and financial data.

 - Excellent analytical, communication, and cross-functional partnership skills.

 - Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and execute effectively in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Experience in one or more of the following areas is valuable; candidates are not expected to bring all of them:

 - Inventory, cost, manufacturing, or supply chain accounting, including inventory valuation, standard costing, manufacturing variances, overhead allocation, rebates and buy/sell etc.

 - Accounting supporting hardware, infrastructure, data centers, electronics, robotics, semiconductors, or other capital-intensive operations.

 - Work with contract manufacturers, global supply chains, hardware product launches, or manufacturing scale-up.

 - Oracle Fusion, particularly Costing and Inventory modules, or comparable ERP implementation and process improvement experience.

 - CPA and/or public accounting background.

 - Experience in a high-growth technology environment or building and leading accounting teams.

This role will play a foundational part in building the accounting infrastructure that supports the next generation of AI hardware products. You will help shape the systems, policies, controls, and operational processes that enable scalable manufacturing operations, reliable financial reporting, and launch readiness as the business rapidly grows.

title: EDA Cloud & Developer Infrastructure Engineer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, our custom silicon program, the team works across silicon architecture, RTL design, verification, physical design, systems software, and infrastructure to deliver highly performant, efficient, and scalable hardware solutions.

The Silicon & Systems team brings together hardware and software engineers to co-design and build the next generation of AI infrastructure. We operate at the intersection of silicon, systems, and software, tackling complex technical challenges across the full hardware development lifecycle, from early architecture and design through validation, deployment, and production.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Infrastructure Software Engineer to build and scale the infrastructure and developer workflows that power OpenAI’s custom silicon development. You’ll work closely with engineering teams across design verification, physical design, emulation, formal verification, and systems software to develop reliable, automated, and efficient workflows that accelerate hardware development.

In this role, you'll own and improve the cloud infrastructure, high-performance computing (HPC) environments, CI/CD pipelines, regression systems, and data platforms that support our silicon engineering teams. You'll translate complex hardware development requirements into scalable infrastructure solutions, reducing manual overhead, improving reliability, and enabling engineers to iterate faster.

This is a highly collaborative, hands-on role with opportunities to drive improvements across the entire hardware development lifecycle. We're looking for engineers who bring deep expertise in one or more infrastructure domains, strong software engineering fundamentals, and an interest in expanding their impact across the broader platform.

In this role, you will:

 - Build developer tools and workflows: Partner with hardware engineering teams to understand their development processes, identify bottlenecks, and build tooling, services, and APIs that automate workflows and accelerate engineering productivity.

 - Develop and scale regression infrastructure: Design, implement, and operate large-scale regression systems spanning job scheduling, execution, results collection, triage, and reporting, with a focus on performance, reliability, and reproducibility.

 - Own CI/CD infrastructure: Build and maintain automated pipelines for infrastructure, developer tooling, and cluster configurations, enabling safe deployments, testing, and continuous improvement.

 - Scale cloud and HPC environments: Design, provision, and operate cloud infrastructure and high-performance compute clusters, optimizing scheduling, capacity, reliability, and cost efficiency to support demanding silicon development workloads.

 - Build data infrastructure and observability: Develop data pipelines, databases, and monitoring systems that provide visibility into regression results, infrastructure health, resource utilization, and engineering efficiency.

 - Drive platform reliability and operational excellence: Troubleshoot complex infrastructure issues, improve monitoring and alerting, automate recovery processes, and build systems that are resilient, maintainable, and scalable.

 - Collaborate across hardware and software teams: Work directly with engineers across RTL, verification, physical design, emulation, and software to continuously improve the infrastructure supporting OpenAI's silicon development.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have strong software engineering fundamentals, with proficiency in Python or a similar programming language and experience building reliable automation, tools, or infrastructure services.

 - Bring deep technical expertise in at least one area of infrastructure engineering, such as Linux/HPC environments, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD systems, storage, networking, or EDA development workflows.

 - Have experience designing, deploying, and operating cloud infrastructure, preferably Azure, with familiarity in infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform or Bicep.

 - Have strong Linux systems knowledge, including processes, filesystems, networking, permissions, performance troubleshooting, and system administration.

 - Have experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using tools such as Jenkins, Buildkite, GitHub Actions, or similar platforms.

 - Are comfortable debugging complex distributed infrastructure problems, identifying root causes, and implementing durable solutions.

 - Enjoy working closely with engineering teams to understand technical requirements and translate them into scalable, practical infrastructure solutions.

 - Take ownership of systems end to end, from initial design and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and ongoing operational improvements.

 - Bring strong technical judgment, clear communication, and a collaborative approach to solving ambiguous engineering challenges.

 - Are curious about hardware development and excited to expand your technical expertise across infrastructure, silicon design workflows, and developer productivity.

Bonus Qualifications

 - Experience supporting ASIC or semiconductor development environments, including EDA workflows, design verification, physical design, emulation, or formal verification.

 - Experience operating large-scale HPC clusters or workload schedulers such as Slurm.

 - Familiarity with compute farms, regression frameworks, build systems, and hardware development toolchains.

 - Experience with enterprise identity and authentication systems, such as Entra ID, OpenLDAP, FreeIPA, or SSSD.

 - Experience designing and operating relational databases such as PostgreSQL or MySQL, including schema design, migrations, query optimization, and backups.

 - Familiarity with distributed systems components, including message queues, caching layers, artifact storage, and backend services.

 - Experience with high-performance storage systems, data movement optimization, or large-scale compute infrastructure.

 - Experience managing EDA license servers, license utilization, or other shared infrastructure resources in hardware development environments.

title: Director, Quality
description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.
Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.
We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.
What You Will Do:
In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.
This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.
What you'll bring
15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.
Preferred qualifications
Experience with both product quality and supplier or manufacturing quality, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively across both domains.
Experience with batteries, electronics, sensors, RF systems, precision mechanics, adhesives, miniaturized assemblies, or other demanding product technologies.
Experience leading quality for products that combine hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-enabled member experiences.
Experience building or scaling quality management systems during rapid company growth.
Familiarity with product safety, regulatory, compliance, traceability, and risk-management requirements relevant to wearable technology.
Experience with supplier development, APQP, PPAP, SCAR processes, multi-source strategies, capacity expansion, or major manufacturing transitions.
Experience working across multiple countries, engineering sites, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

description:

You will champion product quality and the user experience by ensuring every ring meets Oura’s rigorous standards for health accuracy, reliability, and jewelry-like craftsmanship. You will establish and improve quality systems at CMs, ensuring robust data collection and analysis to support critical program decisions and long-term supply chain improvements.

Support New Product Introduction (NPI) through FATP development builds, ramp-up, and product launch / mass production

Identify and effectively communicate design and process risks, using data-driven approaches to facilitate discussions and improvements across Oura teams and suppliers
Analyze and evaluate data to establish appropriate sub-assembly / system level spec limits including cosmetic, dimensional, functional/reliability as well as establish process controls limits
Validate that CM processes produce units that meet cosmetic, reliability, and functional design intent.
You are a technical leader who refuses to compromise on the user experience. You understand that “shippable” isn't just about passing a functional test, but about meeting the high aesthetic and reliability standards our customers expect.

7+ years of experience working in a Product Quality, Supplier Manufacturing, Manufacturing Quality Engineer, or Process Engineer role. - - - Ideally seeking someone with strong mechanical process development and design understanding

Experience with quality engineering in high volume hand held / wearable and/or consumer products manufacturing with high cosmetic standards
Experience qualifying and auditing manufacturing processes including PSA/HAF attach, epoxy dispense/molding/curing, and solder/hotbar/laser weld
Experience developing robust IQC / IPQC / OQC controls, including AOI & cosmetics, sampling plans, qualification criteria, SOP/MSOP, CQA, OBA, and dimensional control
Understanding of quality principles and tools such as GRR, CRR, SPC, FA/CA, FMEA, and DOEs.
Understanding of manufacturing/design principles and tools such as DFM, GD&T, and Six Sigma methodologies for variability reduction

title: Lead Functional Safety Engineer
description:
ABOUT STANDARD BOTS

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.



ABOUT THE ROLE

*We're hiring a Lead, but if you're a strong functional safety engineer at Senior, Staff or Principal level, we still want to hear from you. We'll level the role and the offer to the person.

If you want a mature process to run, this isn't the role. If you want to build the safety organization behind the best cobot in the world, with the authority to do it, read on.

Standard Bots arms work right next to people, installed by customers who may have never set up a robot before, with no cage and no integrator's risk assessment to lean on. The robot has to be safe by design, and you'll be the one who proves it.

We want to build the best collaborative robot in the world, and that's impossible without building the safest one: a robot anyone can put next to their people on day one and trust. Most of the industry treats safety as paperwork at the end. We want it to be the thing our robots are known for — designed in from the first sketch and proven on real hardware.

Until now, safety has lived inside our hardware, firmware and test teams, like it does at most young companies that ship. That got our first robots out the door. It won't carry what's next: volume growing fast, several new products in development, and AI changing how robots are taught. So we're pulling safety into one strong team with its own mandate — and that team needs a leader.



📍 LOCATION

Glen Cove, New York, is where our robots are built and tested and where the team's center of gravity sits, so this role requires 5 days/week onsite.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - The safety case. You own it across our products — analysis, architecture, and the certification plan that gets each robot through third-party assessment.

 - The relationship with assessors. You're our technical voice toward notified bodies and NRTLs, and you're the one in the room defending the argument.

 - Verification on real robots. Every safety function gets tested on hardware you trust, fault injection included. You stay hands-on — this is not a reviewing job.

 - The team. You hire and lead the functional safety engineers who join after you, starting with one who leans electronics and controls and one who leans software.

 - Safety in the design, not at the gate. You report to the Head of System Architecture and work daily with hardware, embedded firmware and test. Safety sits in design reviews from the first sketch.


YOUR FIRST YEAR

 - You've owned a safety case for a shipping robot and defended it to an external assessor.

 - Every safety function has a verification on real hardware that you trust, including fault injection.

 - Your decisions are in the safety architecture of our next generation of arms.

 - Hardware and firmware engineers come to you early, because it saves them time.

 - You've built a team that runs without you in the room, and set how Standard Bots works on safety.



WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - You've taken collaborative robots, or machinery of similar complexity, through third-party safety assessment — and you can tell us what went wrong.

 - You work fluently in ISO 10218-1 and -2, ISO 13849-1 and -2, ISO 12100 and IEC 61508, and you have an opinion on the 2025 revision of ISO 10218.

 - You can read a schematic and a firmware architecture well enough to challenge the engineers who wrote them.

 - You know the full toolkit (FMEA, FTA, HAZOP, STPA, SISTEMA) and which one to reach for.

 - You'd rather be on the test floor with a robot and a force gauge than in a document review.

 - You know the difference between what the standard requires and what actually makes the robot safe, and you deliver both.

 - For the Lead seat: you've led or mentored safety engineers, or you're ready to build a team for the first time.

You don't need to tick every box. If you're close — at any level — apply anyway. We'd rather meet you.

Nice to have

 - You've worked on the assessor side, at a notified body or NRTL.

 - You know mobile manipulators and AMRs: ANSI/RIA R15.08, ISO 3691-4.

 - You've built or specified a safety controller rather than bought one.

 - You've shipped at a startup and liked it.



COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

The salary range for this role is $170,000 - $230,000, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: Data Scientist, FX Quantitative Research
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data scientists and data analysts learn and grow together. The Treasury Finance Data Science team builds the models, risk frameworks, and decision tools behind how Stripe manages money at global scale: liquidity, funding, counterparty risk, and foreign exchange.
Stripe moves funds across 135+ currencies every day. That creates FX exposure from merchant flows, multi-currency balances, and entity funding. In this role, you'll be a thought partner and builder alongside Stripe's FX team. Together you'll develop the quantitative foundation for how Stripe measures, forecasts, and hedges FX exposure.
What you'll do
You'll be the senior quantitative lead for FX within Treasury Finance Data Science. You'll co-build with Treasury, the FX hedging team, Finance, and Engineering: shaping the research agenda, turning ideas into rigorous models, and building the systems that put those models to work. Data Science owns these systems. They produce the decision-critical outputs and analyses that the FX team and Treasury leadership rely on. This is a hands-on role. title: Lead Performance Drilling Engineer
location: United States of America - Texas - Houston; United States of America - Colorado - Denver
description:

Job Description:
bpx energy, a major oil and gas producer in the United States, leverages its expertise in unconventional gas, including shale, to deliver hydrocarbon production and technical knowledge worldwide. With operations in Texas and Louisiana, our US onshore business has become both a premier oil and gas producer and a leader in reducing methane emissions.
As part of BP, a global industry leader, we foster a high-energy, high-intensity environment built on accountability, collegiality, innovation, and empowerment. Discover your place with us and help our business meet the challenges of reimagining and reinventing the future of energy.
Role Synopsis
The Performance Drilling Engineer will be responsible for the safe optimization of and improvements in ft/day and $/ft within drilling. They will work with engineering peers, well site supervisors, remote operations center, and subsurface team members to achieve this goal. The focus of the Performance Team is to work with the team to deliver improvements in on bottom and flat time metrics with impactful gains to the Drilling organization. They are expected to demonstrate by action good technical judgment, professionalism, one team spirit, leadership skills in promoting a safe operation at the well site and together with the Team to drill safe and compliant wells in bpx energy.
Key Accountabilities
The Performance Drilling Engineer will work with engineering and field execution teams to design and execute safe, technically sound, and cost-effective drilling projects. Performance Drilling Engineer is responsible for the technical performance improvements withing the drilling program and will support execution of various drilling performance projects across the company.
Drive Continuous Improvement based on standardization as key to deliver overall operational reliability and consistency.
Analyzing and diagnosing drilling inefficiencies and making parameter / BHA recommendations.
Thorough identification of risks and mitigating controls for all recommended procedures - includes risk assessments, MOCs, and ensuring alignment with corporate, regulatory, and asset standards.
Work with Drilling Engineers, Drilling Superintendents, cross functional team members, and vendors to solve problems and identify continuous improvement opportunities.
Excellent communication and presentation skills, including preparing and presenting information to peers and cross functional teams.
Secure bids for services from reputable and approved sub-contractors. Engage competent and qualified contractors that work to a company standard of operational and safety performance.
Conduct research on offset wells, evaluate new ideas and drilling technics. Be open and willing to aggressively seek better methods and techniques of drilling wells.
Manage a variable workload as rig activity rises and falls based on the goals of the company.
Communicate effectively, treat all employees and contractors with respect, promote safe, inclusive, and engaging environment.
Essential Experience and Education
BS degree in Engineering from an accredited (USA accreditation standard) university. Preferred degrees are Petroleum, Mechanical or Civil Engineering.
Experience as a Drilling Engineer for 8 or more years with an independent or major oil company in similar capacity. Work experience with an industry service provider is a plus.
Experience with computer software for modelling casing design, directional well plan, hydraulics, torque & drag.
Have detailed and demonstrated technical knowledge of drilling horizontal wells.
Engineering and operational experience in drilling including casing design, directional drilling, drill string/BHA design, drilling fluids, cementing, and contingency planning.
A strong awareness of the critical factors that affect performance such as rock mechanical properties, drill bits, drilling fluids, downhole drilling vibration and BHA /performance components.
Excellent communication and presentation skills required along with a high-energy personality.
Have industry training, such as WC Certification, Murchison, Extended Reach drilling or similar courses is preferred.
Ability to develop ideas and technical proposals with minimal supervision.
Track record optimizing drilling performance and promoting continuous improvement.
Demonstrate an aggressive ability to seek new and more efficient ways to improve drilling performance.
Understand and demonstrate leadership in all aspects of managing an HSE compliant operation without sacrificing operational efficiency.
Familiar with data analytics tools and basic programming skills.
